text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Kabariti assures head of U.N. agency for Palestinian refugees that Jordan is committed to helping either return the refugees or compensate them.
- Parliament's financial and economic committee to finish discussions on draft customs law soon.
- Tender in March for second mobile phone network.
- Cabinet approves Iraqi oil supply agreement and 1997 trade protocol with Baghdad.
- Iraqi sources say Iraqi leadership decided five weeks ago to reconsider slain defector Hussein Kamel as "Martyr of the Tribal Fury".
- Japanese government expected to offer $80 million grant to help Jordan get water allocation from Israel.
- Minister of Supply Sobar says food prices will not go up when private sector starts importing.
- Bomb detectors installed at Amman airport and main post offices after recent wave of letter bombs to Al-Hayat newspaper.
